column115: 3G  The Ministry of Civil Affairs recently issued ‘The Guidelines for the Prevention and Control of COVID-19 in Elderly Care Facilities (Version One).’   The notice included 6 aspects of measures: organization and leadership, access management, psychological comfort, elderly protection, internal control, and common disinfectants. According to the guidelines, care facilities are required to 1) reduce entry and exit of people by banning some unnecessary visitors and recording information of necessary visitors, 2) quarantine returning workers and newly admitted elderly, 3) clean and sanitize daily, and 4) conduct temperature tests on elderly daily    https://web.archive.org/web/20200813142904/http://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2020-01/28/content_5472755.htm

On January 29, Hubei Provincial Civil Affairs Department announced that all LTCF for the elderly people should execute temporarily closed management, requring that:  1. Cancel all visits and gatherings. Relatives of their children are encouraged to use wechat, videos and phone calls to console the elderly. LTCFs are not allowed to accept new elderly residents before the epidemic is over.  2. Pay daily attention to the health conditions of elderly people. The body temperature of elderly people and staff should be measured twice a day; Windows should be opened regularly for ventilation, and hospital disinfection should be carried out regularly to maintain environmental hygiene in the institution.  3. Home care services for the elderly in urban and rural communities will be suspended. All home-based elderly care service organizations in the province should suspend door-to-door service projects for the elderly, and all street day care centers for the elderly, urban and rural community home care centers, meals for the elderly and other service facilities should be temporarily closed.  4. Strengthen personal protection for staff in elderly care institutions. Staff of institutions should strictly implement prevention and control systems such as disinfection and temperature measurement on their daily commute. Elderly care workers who have returned to work from middle-risk areas should be quarantined at home for 14 days.  https://archive.vn/n88Nr

column103: On March 18,  National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China issued a guidance on mask wearing. Medical masks and surgical masks are sufficient for normal use, and wearing multiple masks does not provide more protection, according to the guideline. The public is advised to carry along masks when in crowded places such as offices, shopping malls, restaurants, workshops and public transport. People in high-risk areas should wear surgical masks all the time when entering such places, while those in medium-risk and low-risk areas need to wear medical masks when in contact with others at the distance of less than 1 meter. Those who have cold symptoms such as coughing or sneezing, or who live with personnel in quarantine or that have recovered from the novel coronavirus and been discharged from the hospital, are suggested to wear disposable medical or surgical masks. People working in places such as hospitals, train terminals, airports, prisons and nursing homes need to wear surgical masks or respirators of grade KN95/N95 or above. The suspected cases, confirmed cases of novel coronavirus, asymptomatic cases and those who have close contact with confirmed cases are recommended to wear surgical masks or respirators with no breathing valve graded at KN95/N95 or above. Entry personnel need to wear such masks from the moment they enter the country to the end of their required quarantine.    See National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China website, archived:   http://archive.today/2020.10.19-223608/http://www.nhc.gov.cn/jkj/s3577/202003/0a472cc09e744144883db6a74fe6e760.shtml    See Zhejiang Daily website, archived:   https://web.archive.org/web/20210214055653/http://zjrb.zjol.com.cn/html/2020-03/19/content_3315711.htm?div=-1

column106: This extended note aims to capture the progress on vaccination programme before it is rolled out to the entire country (does not include R&D, clinic trials).    The China National Medicine Products Administration (MPA) has not formally approved the Sinopharm Inactivated vaccine to go to the market. However, the green light is anticipated in the next few days.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214212000/https://weareunited.com.my/11515744/    On 24 June 2020, the MPA approved the emergency use of COVID-19 vaccine. Voluntary vaccination started on around 17 June. The first batch of receivers consisted mainly of key workers, including state-owned enterprise employees who must go overseas to countries where the pandemic hits hard; medical staff, epidemic-control staff, border force and other essential workers who keep cities running.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231804/https://finance.sina.com.cn/chanjing/cyxw/2020-11-18/doc-iiznezxs2537217.shtml    From mid-October, Zhejiang province has offered vaccines to ordinary citizens on a voluntary basis. The rationale has been that many cities in Zhejiang have export-oriented economies; for example, Yiwu city is the world centre for light industry commodity trading. Many wholesale merchants were keen on receiving vaccines so that they can travel to Latin America and Africa to inspect their businesses. See BBC reports below. By mid-November, Zhejiang had provided vaccines to some 743,000 people. Voluntary vaccines were paid by recipients. Two doses cost roughly 400 CNY plus a service charge of around 56 CNY, which altogether equals to approximately 70 USD.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231741/https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/simp/chinese-news-54628714    As the vaccination programme is yet to roll out to the whole country, there is no national policy on who will get the vaccine first. However, Sichuan province, where the most recent cluster of infection was found, did publish a detailed plan to that sets out the order:    The first group to receive vaccines consists of people facing high risks of infection, including medical staffs with International assistance mission, national health emergency rescue team in Sichuan, fever clinic and frontline doctors and nurses, border control force, frontline health inspection and epidemic-control officials, students or workers going overseas, police force, frozen food industry workers, essential workers for keeping cities running, teachers, other medical staffs, doctors and nurses, community social workers. The first batch is estimated to have 2 million people. Vaccination for them has started and will finish within 2020.    The second group to receive vaccines mainly consists of vulnerable people, including elderly people and people with chronic diseases. Vaccination for them will start from early next year (January).    The third batch will open to the general public. Ordinary people are estimated to start receiving vaccines after the Chinese New Year (12 February 2021).    http://web.archive.org/web/20201214221555/https://www.sohu.com/a/437018675_114988    So far, vaccination is not and is unlike to be paid by social medical insurance funds in the future. The National Health Security Administration has cited laws and regulations as the justification that vaccination is a part of public health effort, which should be shouldered by public finance resources, rather than social medical insurance funds.     http://web.archive.org/web/20201214211226/https://www.sohu.com/a/425495553_114986    UAE and Bahrain have formally approved the Sinopharm vaccine on 9th and 13th December 2020 respectively.    http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231619/http://www.xinhuanet.com/2020-12/09/c_1126842251.htm  http://web.archive.org/web/20201214231549/http://www.xinhuanet.com/world/2020-12/14/c_1126855787.htm
